guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, timer_expired is cleared to 0.
When rst_ni is high and timer_update is asserted, timer_expired is cleared to 0, overriding any other condition.
When rst_ni is high, timer_update is low, timer_enable is high, and timer_value equals all zeros, timer_expired is set to 1.
When none of the explicit conditions apply (rst_ni high, timer_update low, and not (timer_enable && timer_value == 0)), timer_expired retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: When timer_enable is high, timer_value == '0 means the external timer has reached its terminal count (i.e., truly expired).
assumptions.risk: If timer_value can be zero at a time that does not correspond to expiry (e.g., premature reset, incorrect counting), timer_expired will be set spuriously, causing downstream logic to act on a false expiry.

assumptions.claim: timer_update must be asserted externally after a true timer expiration to clear timer_expired and allow subsequent expiry events to be detected.
assumptions.risk: If timer_update is never asserted, timer_expired stays high permanently, potentially stalling or misleading consumers that expect a one‑shot expiry indication.

uncertain_points.claim: When both timer_update and (timer_enable && timer_value == 0) are true at the same time, the code clears timer_expired instead of setting it; it is unclear if this concurrent condition can occur and what the intended behavior is.
uncertain_points.risk: If both conditions can legally coincide, a real expiration could be missed, potentially breaking protocol timing (e.g., entropy accumulation timeout) or causing safety/security violations.
